card.name: Inside split-up names and capitalized words
card.fires_on: Partway through a rare or unusual word that is split into pieces. Examples are all-caps words (DIMINISHED, PRECAUTIONS, AUGUSTORUM), transliterated names with an apostrophe-like mark (Ko‘olau, Shar‘ah), and long medical names (bilirubinemia, avancin).

modes.label: Okina or apostrophe in names
modes.description: A curly apostrophe-like mark inside a transliterated Hawaiian or Arabic name.

modes.label: All-caps words split up
modes.description: A middle piece of an all-caps heading or inscription word.

modes.label: Medical or brand names
modes.description: A middle piece of a lab term or drug brand name.

card.plain: It fires in the middle of an unusual word that has been cut into pieces, such as a capitalized heading or a foreign name.
